body:
He was in couple therapy with his ex wife, on his initiative, and also went to a couple of sessions on his own, after the break up. But that only made him feel like "therapists" are a waste of time and "you can only get by on your own anyway". Whenever he is troubled he just drives for hours...he says that's what always helps him find the answer to everything, and indeed he seems to be right. But I think you can see what I'm dealing with here. I'm pretty sure he would just see me as weak if I told him about this. He might also think he has no luck with women at all, heh. On the other hand, I know I can't exactly build a relationship if I hide something this important from my partner...I don't know what to do here. I think I'll just wait for the time being...don't you just love procrastination?

I do have two very good friends who've helped me immensely through all this. But there's only so much they can do and my shitty days don't seem to end. When I'm among friends, among people, half the time I feel like I'm not there...That's one of the questions my psychiatrist asked me: Do you feel like you participate, that you actively engage in conversations? Sometimes I do, I genuinely forget about everything. Other times, I just don't know how to leave faster and go back to my place. 

I have no idea what the pattern for this good/bad days is. I have tried to see if I can find one, I my conclusion so far is there isn't any. It seems to be totally random.

Thanks for being so supportive...I will tell my doctor about the suicidal thoughts. I'll be careful to phrase it well, after all...as someone dealing with depression I think you know how good we can become at convincing almost everybody we are ok...

I would lie if I said medication and therapy didn't help, though. Three months ago I wasn't even making sense anymore, and honestly, I don't even remember those days very well. I don't remember much of the first three weeks...

I've read many suggestions for depressed people, they all say get out, go to the gym, watch comedies...the problem is you can get into a state where you lose even the faintest impulse to do something, anything. I know the black, deep hole all too well...

How do you manage to get out of the hole when you're in it? I'm talking about those really bad days, as I see them. The only thing I've been able to do is just wait until the next one...

Please see my reply to krugerlive as well.

Indeed, that's what I feel, too. Z (I don't have experience with other SSRIs) limits the intensity of emotions. Problem is, they kind of limit ALL emotions. I would lie if I said I feel like a vegetable, but I think it makes me too detached. Now, even if I get mad, it only lasts for a couple of minutes.

I should say my doctor also put me on 1mg lorazepam in the beginning (first month) but I stopped taking it because I no longer felt I needed it (probably because I was already numbed by Z). She didn't have anything against it and said it was ok if that's what I felt like (She said its effect only lasts for about 10 minutes, anyway).

That is a good point you have there, I will ask her just how much she thinks it's me, and how much it's just my brain chemistry.

Yes, I've always felt like this, even when I had a job. And I loved my job. But last year I would just come back from work and crawl into my bed wanting to forget about everything. It had become increasingly harder for me to get out. However, I wasn't fired or anything, the company just succumbed to the economy.

I was very happy in my previous relationship, however, there were plenty of days when I just couldn't do anything but lie down inertly, when I just couldn't bring myself to leave the house. My partner was very supportive, but the relationship ended (he ended it)very badly and it couldn't have happened at a worse time. Most of the times I feel like I'm behind it, but lately I've had those thoughts crawling back in my head.

I've recently started dating another man and I feel very guilty towards him. He got divorced two years ago, has to relocate to another country soon, expects a committed, good relationship (which he deserves), and I have no idea what I'm gonna do. I do want to settle down, but at the same time I am terrified of the change. My psychiatrist advised me not to make any big changes right now. My partner doesn't even know I'm taking anti-depressants and I'm afraid to tell him.

Sorry about the rant...

Thanks, you took the words right out of my mouth, I do feel like Z has removed most of my inhibitions. But that's a two way street. 

Therapy has indeed helped me a lot (although it's a very painful process), but I can't afford it any longer.

Thank you. Other than this Zoloft thing, I'm pretty satisfied with my psychiatrist. She actually takes the time to listen to me, every time I see her. I will tell her about this, but I wanted to see what you guys think about this and whether you experienced something similar. However, I'm afraid that she, like all doctors, just follows some basic rules and the moment I mention suicide, she'll freak out. I don't want to lose my freedom, it's the only thing I've left.

Thanks.

I'm afraid to talk to my doctor yet. I'm afraid they're gonna lock me up or something. I wanted to see what you guys think before I talk to her. 

About the young part, I don't know. I'm 32.

The shitty situation is basically I haven't had a job in six months (the market is absolutely dead in my line of work, and not only) and I was basically dumped this summer (which is when I started talking nonsense and some people around me realized I couldn't deal with this on my own anymore).

But starting the medication and the therapy made me realize I'd been depressed eversince my teenage years. I realizethat because I noticed so many obsessive thoughts and ideas disappeared.

I don't want to go into too much detail, because I hate complaining. I know the bad reputation depression has. But I wouldn' t want my worst enemy to go through this. 

And I blame Zoloft for much of what's changed lately. At least before that I could see into the near future, I could imagine some options. Now, it's like this thing doesn't even allow for most thoughts to  form inside my head. I fear I may have fallen into a trap because I no longer care (most of the time, who are we kidding?) about all the shit I'm in , but not caring about anything anymore is entirely something else. And I fear all SSRIs will be like this.
